subtype: Approach: reviewing progress and ending gracefully [Revision]
passage: Saturday. Six months since I started meeting Sangeeta, so today's session was a review. We went through the list from January. Done: portfolio site, two mock interviews, and a first proper offer letter. Not done: the open-source contribution. Sangeeta said she still wants it, so it stays, but on her own with a check-in from me. Then I raised the thing I'd been putting off: maybe we don't need regular sessions anymore. I worried it would sound like I was pulling away. Sangeeta grinned and said she'd been thinking the same and would rather message me when stuck. So we're moving to one catch-up every two months, plus messages anytime. Strange, but it feels like a finish line, not a door closing. — Naveen

qa.a: The open-source contribution was not finished.

qa.q: What did Naveen worry about when raising the change?
qa.a: Naveen worried that it would sound like Naveen was pulling away.

qa.q: What other step could Naveen offer Sangeeta after regular sessions end?
qa.a: Naveen could offer a one-off session before any big decision, such as a job choice, since it keeps support available without a fixed rota.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta see the move to occasional check-ins?
qa.a: Sangeeta probably sees it as a good step, since she had been thinking the same and would rather message when stuck.

grounding: Shows a mentor and mentee reviewing goals achieved after six months and agreeing to occasional check-ins, treating the end of regular sessions as success.
